messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in New York with reading room and fiction section, in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and children section, and in Chicago with cafe and reading room. We need to use the function public_library_find_nearby. The function signature: location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to call the function three times with appropriate parameters. The facilities parameter expects a single value or an array? The description says "Facilities and sections in public library." It lists options: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That suggests that facilities can be one of those strings or an array of strings? The type is ambiguous. But likely we need to pass an array of strings for multiple facilities. The function expects a single string or array? The type is union of string or array? The description: "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". That means facilities can be one of those strings or an array of strings? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Maybe they want to pass an array of strings. Let's pass an array of strings for each query.

So first call: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Second: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Third: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to output the function calls. Use the function tool.
